solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cleaner thus hoovers up half of village post office (7)

indicators.note: a vacuum cleaner sucks things inside itself, so SO takes in the letters that follow
take one half of the word: HAM from HAMLET

blocks.note: the first half of HAMLET, a small village

annotation.surface: A cleaner vacuuming her way through the village post office.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the cleaner a person pushing a Hoover; the definition is the product itself, as in carpet shampoo.
annotation.definitionFit: Named by function: shampoo is a detergent used to wash hair or carpets, so a cleaner in the product sense.

entries.clue: What might have pumped bullet ultimately into military leader? (7)

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'bullet'
a bullet fired into someone ends up inside them, so T is put inside SHOGUN

blocks.note: the shogun was Japan's military ruler

annotation.surface: A bullet being pumped into a general, as if in a shooting.
annotation.walkthrough: A pump-action shotgun is worked by pumping the fore-end, which is why the definition is 'what might have pumped'; the question mark flags that loose sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A pump-action shotgun is pumped between shots, so it is something that might have pumped.

entries.clue: Evidence when waiting for the train, hours slipping away (11)

indicators.note: the H for hours leaves the phrase

blocks.note: where you wait for a train: at the station

annotation.surface: Someone's alibi: they were waiting for a train as the hours passed.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole phrase AT THE STATION is written out, then its H drops out, and the word breaks leave ATTESTATION.
annotation.definitionFit: An attestation is evidence or a formal statement that something is true.

entries.clue: Captive to arouse great enthusiasm in discussion (6)

blocks.note: to wow an audience is to thrill it

annotation.surface: A prisoner wins over the room during a debate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins the wordplay to the definition here; it is not putting anything inside anything.
annotation.definitionFit: Originally a Native American council meeting, the word is now informal English for any get-together to talk things over.

entries.clue: Exact location of the King’s Head? (2,3,5)

blocks.note: taken literally: a monarch's head is printed on coins and notes

annotation.surface: Directions to a pub called the King's Head.
annotation.walkthrough: The King's Head reads as a pub name, but it is the monarch's head printed on coins and notes, so its location is on the money.
annotation.definitionFit: 'On the money' means exactly right.

entries.clue: Slavic rider’s bag of lettuce? (7)

blocks.note: cos is a type of lettuce (romaine)

annotation.surface: A horseman carrying a bag of lettuce.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is': a Slavic rider is a 'cos sack', a bag of lettuce, and the question mark admits it.
annotation.definitionFit: Cossacks were famous horsemen of the Russian and Ukrainian steppes.

entries.clue: County seal (4)

blocks.note: a county in the south of the Republic of Ireland
the thing pushed into a wine bottle's neck to seal it

annotation.walkthrough: Cork is a county in the Republic of Ireland; a cork is also what seals a bottle.
annotation.definitionFit: Cork is an Irish county, and a cork seals a bottle.

entries.clue: Prominence of unusual case circumventing legal right (8)

indicators.note: CASE is not in its usual order, so its letters are rearranged
the rearranged CASE goes round LIEN

blocks.note: anagram of CASE, split around LIEN
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

annotation.surface: A notable court case that sidesteps a legal right.
annotation.walkthrough: The legal surface makes 'case' look like a lawsuit; it is just four letters to shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something salient sticks out, from Latin for leaping, so its salience is how prominent it is.

entries.clue: Idiot equally soft in the head (3)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Calling someone an idiot who is just as soft in the head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soft in the head' reads as the idiom for foolish, but it is the first letter of 'soft'.
annotation.definitionFit: The donkey's reputation for stupidity made its name an insult for a foolish person, a plain synonym for idiot.

entries.clue: Sauce finished at bottom of vessel (7)

indicators.note: in a down answer, UP sits below KETCH

blocks.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

annotation.surface: Leftover sauce at the bottom of a bowl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a bowl or bottle for the sauce; it is a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the tomato condiment on every café table is one kind of sauce.

entries.clue: Opening of olfactory organ a lot (3)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'olfactory'

blocks.note: a newspaper is an organ; FT = the Financial Times

annotation.surface: A nose, the olfactory organ, opening wide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Olfactory organ' reads as one phrase for the nose; split it, and 'organ' is a newspaper, the FT.
annotation.definitionFit: Oft is an old word for often, a lot.

entries.clue: Scotsman of power has Queen shut in throne room! (5,6)

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so WATT holds the rest inside it
'shut in' reads as locked up, and here ER CLOSE is placed within WATT

blocks.note: James Watt, Scottish engineer; the watt is the unit of power

annotation.surface: A powerful Scot locks the Queen in the throne room.
annotation.walkthrough: The throne is the toilet seat, so the throne room is the loo, not a royal chamber.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang joke: the toilet seat is called the throne, so the room holding it is the throne room, the WC.

entries.clue: Sanction for use in cigarette lighter (3,5)

indicators.note: OK is put to use inside GASPER

blocks.note: a gasper is British slang for a cheap cigarette

annotation.surface: Approving something to go in a cigarette lighter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cigarette lighter' reads as one object, but the definition is 'lighter' alone; a gas poker is a gas-fed rod once used to light coal fires.
annotation.definitionFit: A gas poker is a device for lighting a fire, so a lighter.

entries.clue: Supply worker with what high-protein food (6)

blocks.note: a temp is a stand-in worker, like a supply teacher

annotation.surface: Asking a supply worker what the high-protein meal is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' sounds like a verb, to supply food; it is part of the job title.
annotation.definitionFit: Tempeh is fermented soybean cake, rich in protein.

entries.clue: Romeo incarcerated by movie villain — King, say? (7,4)

indicators.note: R is locked up inside CAD

annotation.surface: A film where the villain locks up Romeo, perhaps a gangster called King.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Movie villain' reads as one phrase; it is two separate pieces, PICTURE and CAD.
annotation.definitionFit: A king in a pack of cards is a picture card, alongside queen and jack.

entries.clue: Little stuff in grass (10)

indicators.note: stuff that is in the grass sits within it, so MATTER goes inside SING

blocks.note: to grass or sing is to inform on someone

annotation.surface: Tiny things lost in the lawn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is the slang verb to inform, as is 'sing'; nothing to do with lawns.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as in 'a smattering of French': a slight amount, so 'little' in its noun sense, as in 'a little'.

entries.clue: Awesome as it is, landlord! (4)

blocks.note: how you order whisky undiluted, with no ice or mixer

annotation.surface: A customer ordering a drink from the pub landlord.
annotation.walkthrough: A landlord here is a publican: you ask for whisky 'neat', as it is, with nothing added.
annotation.definitionFit: Neat is slang for great, and a neat spirit is served undiluted.

entries.clue: Lousy Constable miniature? (3,4,3)

blocks.note: taken literally: a pint-sized police constable is not much of a cop

annotation.surface: Scorn for a small painting by the artist John Constable.
annotation.walkthrough: Constable seems to be the painter; read as a policeman, a miniature one is not much of a cop. 'Not much cop' is British slang for poor.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Not much cop' means no good, lousy.

entries.clue: Approach sign on end of avenue while driving, seemingly? (4,4)

indicators.note: one thing placed on another is attached to it, so OMEN is joined directly to E
take the last letter of avenue
someone driving is in a car, so the pieces go inside CAR

annotation.surface: A road sign at the end of an avenue as a driver approaches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'While driving' is a cryptic stand-in for 'in a car'; the 'seemingly' and question mark admit it is a loose equivalence.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to move closer to something, as in 'don't come near me'.

entries.clue: Could one be in flat — here? (10)

definitions.text: Could one be in flat — here?

indicators.note: to be in a flat is to be inside it, so IS ONE is placed within MATTE

blocks.note: a matte finish is flat, not glossy
the question 'could one be?' answered: IS ONE

annotation.surface: A question whether someone might live in a flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flat' first reads as the home; it is the paint finish MATTE, while the whole clue also describes the answer, a flat you could be in.
annotation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors, somewhere one could be.

entries.clue: Cooler call from little lamb, by the sound of it? (7)

indicators.note: the answer is spoken like 'mini baa'

annotation.surface: A tiny lamb bleating.
annotation.walkthrough: In British speech BAR and BAA sound the same, with no R said.
annotation.definitionFit: A minibar is a small hotel-room fridge, a cooler for drinks.

entries.clue: Result of knocking back last of lager in bar? (4)

definitions.text: Result of knocking back last of lager in bar?

indicators.note: to knock something back is to send it backwards, so PUB is written back to front
take the last letter of lager
R goes into the turned bar

annotation.surface: Downing the last of a pint in a pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' reads as drinking; it turns PUB round. The whole clue also defines the answer: a burp is what downing lager produces.
annotation.definitionFit: A burp is what gulping beer brings on.

entries.clue: Roast a cook cut in style (7)

indicators.note: CHEF has its last letter cut off

blocks.note: to roast or pan a show is to criticise it harshly

annotation.surface: Roasting meat and carving it with a flourish.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface makes 'roast' a cooking verb; it means to criticise.
annotation.definitionFit: Panache was once a plume on a helmet; it now means dash and flair, the showy sense of style.

entries.clue: Pound plus shilling where the franc is currency (6)

blocks.note: an old British sum of 21 shillings, one more than a pound
a former French colony in West Africa still using a franc

annotation.surface: A currency exchange puzzle about old British money and francs.
annotation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British sum of 21 shillings, a pound (20 shillings) plus one shilling; Guinea is a West African country using the Guinean franc.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: a pre-decimal British coin still used for horse-racing prices, and a country that kept the franc from French rule.

entries.clue: Stake between poles in French city (6)

indicators.note: ANTE sits between N and S

blocks.note: an ante is a poker stake

annotation.surface: A stake planted between poles in a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stake' and 'poles' look like wooden posts; one is a gambling stake, the others are compass points.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the port on the Loire in Brittany's old heartland is one French city among many.

entries.clue: Blue cheese finally introduced to producer of wine list (8)

indicators.note: take the last letter of cheese
to introduce is literally to lead inside, so E is put into CRU

blocks.note: a cru is a wine-producing vineyard
a ship lists when it leans

annotation.surface: Blue cheese added to a wine list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue cheese' and 'wine list' are both false pairings: 'Blue' is the definition and 'list' means lean.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin caeruleus, sky-coloured: a painter's name for one shade, so blue by example.

entries.clue: Housekeeper cooked for the auditor? (4)

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is heard

blocks.note: to make dinner is to cook it

annotation.surface: The housekeeper cooked for the accountant checking the books.
annotation.walkthrough: The auditor seems to be the accountant being fed; it is a listener, hearing MADE as MAID.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the domestic-service sense: a maid is a servant who cleans and runs a household.

entries.clue: Fuelled by oxygen, another bit exploding in blast! (11)

indicators.note: O is fed in with the fodder
the letters are blown apart and rearranged

annotation.surface: An explosion caused by oxygen feeding a fire.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemistry surface hides that 'blast!' is an exclamation of annoyance, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Botheration!' and 'blast!' are both mild curses.

entries.clue: Drop of the hard stuff, little one (3)

annotation.surface: A small child and a nip of whisky.
annotation.walkthrough: A tot is a small measure of spirits and also a small child.
annotation.definitionFit: Tot means both a small dram and a toddler.

entries.clue: Discharge extremists ejected from demonstration (3)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, and ejecting them throws them out

annotation.surface: Hard-liners thrown out of a protest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' look like political radicals; they are the end letters of MARCH.
annotation.definitionFit: An arc is an electrical discharge across a gap.

entries.clue: Left, with flag in appropriate colour? (7)

indicators.note: a flag flying in red is wrapped in that colour, so TIRE sits inside RED

blocks.note: red is the colour of the political left

annotation.surface: A left-wing flag in its proper red.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets 'Left' up as politics; red suits that sense, but the definition is left meaning withdrew.
annotation.definitionFit: Past tense of the verb: to retire is to withdraw from a room or a job, so retired = left.

entries.clue: VIP well stocked with foreign cash? (7)

indicators.note: GEE holds RAND like stock

blocks.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

annotation.surface: A rich VIP with plenty of foreign money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well stocked' reads as one idiom for rich; 'well' is the exclamation GEE.
annotation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank.
